sample_space.shape: cylindrical sample puck, 72 mm sample space, 144 mm long, docked from below onto a cold finger on the BLL-72 Secondary Insert and sitting in the solenoid bore
sample_space.description: Patented bottom loader: the puck is pushed up a vacuum lock from below with a removable loading arm and pressed onto the cold-finger docking interface (make-before-break grounding for ESD). Puck carries 96 DC lines (2 x 51-way Nano-D) and up to 28 SMP coax. 14 T solenoid option; the magnet text gives bores 77-152 mm but does not state the 14 T bore, so the 14 T + 72 mm pairing is undocumented (brochure: 'Dependent on magnet selection').

notes: Scene: vertical aluminium OVC of stacked cylindrical sections on a cross-braced steel frame; inside, top plate -> PT1 (77 K) -> PT2 (4 K copper shield, magnet hangs from it) -> still (700 mK shield) -> cold plate (100 mK) -> 360 mm mixing chamber plate (< 10 mK; MX450 guaranteed > 450 uW at 100 mK, > 12 uW at 20 mK). One Sumitomo RP-182B2S pulse tube (PTR options 1.35/1.50/1.80 W; 1.5 W = RP-182B2S) with separated valve unit. One 117 x 252 mm Secondary Insert slot carries the BLL-72 bottom-loader SI with cold finger: 28 SMA hermetic + 4 x 24-way Fischer at room temperature, 28 SMP + 2 x 51-way Nano-D at the cold finger, plus one spare ISO100 LOS port (up to 37 coax). The 72 mm x 144 mm puck enters from below through a vacuum lock on a removable loading arm; load < 15 min, 10 h cooldown, < 12 mK and 150 uW at 100 mK at the puck. 14 T solenoid, quench protected, ramps to full field in 1 h or less; patented gas-gap heat switches with a remote sorb (outgassed at ~30 K) link the plates. Also 2 x KF40 + 2 x KF25 LOS ports on the top plate. CAVEATS: PT1/PT2/still/cold-plate temperatures and the 2 m x 0.6 m outer size come from the published Sheffield QSHS Proteox MX500 (8 T custom magnet), the closest documented Proteox MX, not an MX450 datasheet. The catalog unknown stands: the 14 T + 72 mm / 28-coax pairing is 'Dependent on magnet selection' and undocumented; the BLL-60 (77 mm bore, 22 coax, 96 DC) may be the actual 14 T puck. A Pisa MX450 (no magnet) is wired with 7 coax, 2 x 24-wire DC looms and 2 single-mode fibres (cisup.unipi.it/?p=5370), a different real-world wiring.
